vulnerabilities.name: MS17-010 EternalBlue
vulnerabilities.description: EternalBlue is an exploit that targets a vulnerability in Microsoft's implementation of the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. It allows remote code execution by sending specially crafted packets to SMBv1 servers. This exploit was part of the NSA tools leaked by the Shadow Brokers group and was used in the WannaCry ransomware attack.
vulnerabilities.danger: Allows unauthenticated remote code execution on SMBv1 servers, enabling malware propagation and complete system compromise

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2017-0144
vulnerabilities.description: CVE-2017-0144 is the formal identifier for the SMBv1 remote code execution vulnerability patched by MS17-010. The vulnerability exists in the SMBv1 server handling of certain requests. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain the ability to execute code on the target server. This is the underlying vulnerability exploited by EternalBlue.
vulnerabilities.danger: Remote code execution vulnerability in SMBv1 that can be chained with EternalBlue for full system compromise

vulnerabilities.name: Log4Shell
vulnerabilities.description: Log4Shell is a critical zero-day vulnerability in Apache Log4j 2, a popular Java logging library. It allows unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted log messages containing JNDI lookup patterns. The vulnerability affects millions of applications worldwide and is considered one of the most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered due to the ubiquitous nature of Log4j.
vulnerabilities.danger: Unauthenticated remote code execution via JNDI injection in Log4j, affecting countless Java applications and services

vulnerabilities.name: EternalRomance
vulnerabilities.description: EternalRomance is another SMB exploit from the Shadow Brokers leak, similar to EternalBlue but targeting a different vulnerability in SMBv1. It exploits a flaw in the SMB transaction handling to achieve remote code execution. EternalRomance is particularly effective against Windows 7 and Server 2008 systems.
vulnerabilities.danger: Remote code execution via SMBv1 transaction handling flaw, providing reliable exploitation of older Windows systems

vulnerabilities.name: Shellshock
vulnerabilities.description: Shellshock (CVE-2014-6271) is a vulnerability in the Bash shell that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via specially crafted environment variables. It affects CGI scripts hosted on web servers that use Bash to process requests, as well as DHCP clients and other services that pass environment variables to Bash.
vulnerabilities.danger: Remote command injection via Bash environment variables, allowing full system compromise of vulnerable servers
